cards.explanation: The answer is heard. David waited patiently, and the LORD inclined to him and heard his cry. I yell at my oven timer all day and it has never once heard me, friends. David's cry reached the LORD, and that's the whole point of the verse.

The answer is upon a rock. David says the LORD set his feet upon a rock. After miry clay, that's a big upgrade, friends. Mud gives way under you, but a rock holds. I'd do a little dance on it, and I'd bring my gold base along.

The answer is False. David says the LORD set his feet upon a rock and made his footsteps firm. No slipping, no sliding, no skating, friends. I've slid off a counter before, and I can tell you firm footing is a gift.

The answer is a new song. David says the LORD put a new song in his mouth, a hymn of praise to our God. Think about that, friends. The LORD lifted him out of the pit, and a song is what gets put in his mouth. I can't carry a tune in a bucket.
The answer is True. David says, “Many will see and fear and put their trust in the LORD.” It comes right after the new song, friends. David isn't the only one in view, because many will see.

The answer is False. David says the blessed man has made the LORD his trust, and has not turned to the proud, nor to those who lapse into falsehood. His trust sits in one place, friends. It doesn't wander around the neighborhood looking for a better offer.

The answer is that they are more than he can count. David says that if he proclaims and declares them, they are more than he can count. I try to count my cookie batches and lose track by Thursday, friends. And that's just a bakery. David is talking about the wonders and plans of the LORD, and he can't get to the end of them.

The answer is that God did not desire or require them. David says, “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but my ears You have opened.” Burnt offerings and sin offerings, he says, God did not require. That's what he says in this verse, friends. I think David is pointing us toward listening.

The answer is that he delights to do it. David says, “I delight to do Your will, O my God; Your law is within my heart.” Delight, friends. That's not a chore on a checklist. It's like me jumping face-first into the chocolate chips, because I enjoy it.

The answer is proclaims. David says, “I proclaim righteousness in the great assembly…” He goes on to say he does not seal his lips, friends. I'd compare him to me holding up a fresh batch and yelling, but he's doing something much better than I am.
The answer is False. David says, “Your loving devotion and faithfulness will always guard me.” Always, friends. I've had a warranty run out on me, and this isn't one of those.

The answer is that his sins have overtaken him so he cannot see. David says, “my sins have overtaken me, so that I cannot see.” That's honest, friends. He doesn't blame anybody else. He names his own sins and says he cannot see.

The answer is hurry. David says, “hurry, O LORD, to help me.” Notice how different that sounds from verse 1, friends. He waited patiently there, and now he's asking for speed. I think that's an honest prayer, because sometimes the need feels urgent.

The answer is that they be ashamed and driven back. David says, “May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; may those who wish me harm be repelled and humiliated.” He's asking the LORD to deal with them, friends. He doesn't say he'll do it himself.

The answer is that they rejoice and be glad in Him. David says, “May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You…” His prayer for the seekers is about joy, friends. I like a prayer that asks for gladness.

The answer is True. David prays that those who love God's salvation will always say, “The LORD be magnified!” It's a prayer for the ones who love the LORD's salvation, friends. I'd say that's a line worth repeating.

The answer is his helper and deliverer. David says, “You are my helper and deliverer; O my God, do not delay.” He starts by calling himself poor and needy, friends. Then he names the LORD as his helper and deliverer. That's a good pairing, because needy folks need a helper.
